CONTEXT
=======
A C++ program /workspace/dataset/earcut.hpp/tests/test7.cpp was ported to pure Rust (std only, edition 2021) in /output.
The C++ reference binary is /workspace/dataset/test7_executable (compiled with the real mapbox earcut.hpp 2.2.x; the
header source itself is NOT on disk and must NOT be sought out - treat it as a black box).

The C++ program: n defaults to 7, overridable by argv[1] parsed with std::atoi. It samples 2*n points of a spiral
(t = i/(n*2), radius = t, angle = 4*M_PI*t, point = (radius*cos(angle), radius*sin(angle))), pushes that single ring
into a polygon, calls mapbox::earcut<uint32_t>(polygon), and prints each returned index followed by a single space
(std::cout << idx << " "), with NO trailing newline. The spiral self-intersects, so earcut's fallback passes
(filterPoints -> cureLocalIntersections -> splitEarcut) are heavily exercised, as is the z-order hashed path once the
total vertex count exceeds 80 (i.e. n > 40).

Rust port layout:
  /output/Cargo.toml
  /output/test7.rs            entry point (uses #[path] module decls so both 'rustc test7.rs' and cargo work)
  /output/src/cli.rs          atoi
  /output/src/spiral.rs       spiral point generation
  /output/src/earcut/mod.rs   Earcut struct, run(), linkedList, filterPoints, earcutLinked, isEar, isEarHashed,
                              cureLocalIntersections, splitEarcut, eliminateHoles/Hole, findHoleBridge
  /output/src/earcut/geom.rs  area, equals, pointInTriangle, sign, onSegment, intersects, intersectsPolygon,
                              locallyInside, middleInside, isValidDiagonal, sectorContainsSector, getLeftmost,
                              splitPolygon, removeNode
  /output/src/earcut/node.rs  Node + NIL sentinel (arena indices replace Node*)
  /output/src/earcut/zorder.rs zOrder, indexCurve, sortLinked

Prebuilt binaries already exist: /output/test7 (rustc -O) and /output/target/release/test7 (cargo).
Already established by the lead engineer (do not redo, but you may spot-check):
  - byte-identical output for every n in 0..=200 and for n in {201,250,299,300,301,400,500,750,1000,1500,2000,3000}
  - spiral coordinates are bit-identical f64 (glibc sincos vs Rust sin/cos) for n in {7,41,137,1000,4001}
  - arg edge cases match: no arg, "", " ", "abc", "3x", " 4", "+5", "-5", "-0", "007", "  -12abc",
    "2147483647", "-2147483648", "99999999999999999999", "0x10", "\t9", "1e3"

DO NOT EDIT ANY FILES. You are read-only: investigate and report. The lead engineer applies fixes.


ADVERSARIAL VERIFICATION (lens: correctness)
=====
A reviewer auditing the Rust port claims:

  file: /output/src/earcut/geom.rs:167
  severity: minor
  summary: sectorContainsSector passes the wrong nodes: it uses `area(m.prev, m, p)` and `area(p.next, m, m.prev)` where earcut.hpp 2.2.x uses `area(m.prev, m, p.prev) < 0 && area(p.next, m, m.next) < 0`. The port never reads `p.prev` or `m.next` at all.
  failure scenario: Any polygon with holes where findHoleBridge's second loop hits an exact `tanCur == tanMin` tie with `p.x <= m.x`, so the `sectorContainsSector(m, p)` disjunct decides the bridge vertex. Reproduced: I built two copies of the module tree differing ONLY in this line (as-is vs. the earcut.hpp form) and ran 400,000 random integer-grid star polygons with 1-3 holes; 146 trials produced different index vectors. Concrete case (from /tmp/h/h3.rs, trial 2566): outer = [[12,0],[8,5],[4,9],[-2,13],[-7,8],[-9,3],[-10,-3],[-5,-6],[-2,-11],[5,-11],[9,-6]], holes = [[-4,-3],[-3,3],[-1,0]], [[1,-3],[-2,-3],[-2,1],[1,1],[1,-1]], [[-4,-3],[-4,0],[-1,-1]] -> as-is emits 51 indices starting `7 8 9 9 10 0 ... 2 2 4 12 2 12 13 17 ...` while the earcut.hpp form emits 54 indices starting `7 8 9 9 10 0 ... 2 13 19 21 21 11 15 ...`. Integer coordinates make the x-intercept arithmetic exact, so this divergence is attributable to sectorContainsSector alone. Holes-only: unreachable from test7's single ring.

Your job is to REFUTE this claim. Read the actual code at that location. Reason from mapbox earcut.hpp 2.2.x semantics. A claim is refuted if the Rust code is in fact equivalent to the C++ (including cases where a rewrite looks different but provably computes the same thing), if the claimed C++ behaviour is misremembered, or if the code path is unreachable for any input this program can produce. Default to refuted=true when uncertain. Set reproduced_divergence=true ONLY if you personally observed the two implementations disagree. DO NOT EDIT FILES under /output.

input.reasoning:
REFUTED — on reachability, which the reviewer themselves concede in the last line of their own report ("Holes-only: unreachable from test7's single ring").

What the code actually says (/output/src/earcut/geom.rs:164-168):

    pub(super) fn sector_contains_sector(&self, m: usize, p: usize) -> bool {
        let mp = self.nodes[m].prev;
        let pn = self.nodes[p].next;
        self.area(mp, m, p) < 0.0 && self.area(pn, m, mp) < 0.0
    }

So the reviewer's reading of the Rust is accurate: it computes area(m.prev, m, p) and area(p.next, m, m.prev), and `p.prev`/`m.next` are never read. Upstream earcut (js 2.2.x and the .hpp port) uses area(m.prev, m, p.prev) < 0 && area(p.next, m, m.next) < 0. The two forms are not algebraically equivalent, so I am not disputing the substance of the discrepancy — I am disputing that it is a defect in this port.

Reachability is the decisive point, and it is airtight static reasoning, not a probabilistic argument:

1. /output/src/earcut/geom.rs:164 has exactly one call site in the whole tree: /output/src/earcut/mod.rs:588, inside find_hole_bridge's second loop (the tan_cur == tan_min tie-break, exactly as the reviewer describes).
2. find_hole_bridge (mod.rs:523) is called from exactly one place: eliminate_hole (mod.rs:507).
3. eliminate_hole (mod.rs:506) is called from exactly one place: eliminate_holes (mod.rs:498).
4. eliminate_holes (mod.rs:471) is called from exactly one place: run (mod.rs:106), and it is guarded by `if points.len() > 1`.
5. /output/test7.rs builds `polygon` with a single `polygon.push(spiral)` and never pushes again, so `points.len() == 1` unconditionally, for every value of n and every argv[1].

Therefore sector_contains_sector is dead code for every input this program can accept. The C++ reference binary's sectorContainsSector is equally never entered, so no argument-ordering difference inside it can produce an observable output difference. There is no argv path that introduces a second ring — n only controls the sample count of the one spiral ring, and the fallback passes the CONTEXT mentions (filterPoints / cureLocalIntersections / splitEarcut) plus the z-order path all live downstream of earcut_linked and never touch find_hole_bridge.

On the reviewer's evidence: their reproduction is not a reproduction of a test7 divergence. They state they built two copies of the module tree and drove them with synthetic "star polygons with 1-3 holes" from /tmp/h/h3.rs — i.e. they constructed a *different* program that calls earcut with multi-ring input, which test7 cannot do. 146/400,000 divergences in a hole-bearing harness says nothing about the port's fidelity on the single-ring input space. I did not attempt to reproduce their harness, and I did not personally observe the two implementations disagree on anything, hence reproduced_divergence=false.

Spot-check confirming no behavioural gap (md5 of stdout, reference vs rustc build vs cargo build), n in {7, 41, 137, 300, 1000} — all three identical at every n, including n=41/137/300/1000 which exercise the hashed z-order path (>80 vertices) and the fallback passes:
  7    a79fed19773deb2e4bf241f17455e76e (x3)
  41   d0fd69c563f14b86ba15ba44ddfe9559 (x3)
  137  0944b933e1f0b92bc77917a43134596b (x3)
  300  c9cf6aa1677db099ceff8dee6190babf (x3)
  1000 1e2a899372ae4d873854f2269586602e (x3)

Verdict: not a correctness defect in this port. At most it is a latent source-fidelity blemish in unreachable code — worth a one-line fix if the lead wants the module tree to be a faithful, reusable earcut translation rather than only a test7-equivalent one, but it cannot change this program's output and should not be reported as a minor correctness finding against the port. Relevant files: /output/src/earcut/geom.rs (lines 164-168), /output/src/earcut/mod.rs (lines 106, 471, 498, 506-507, 523, 588), /output/test7.rs.
